correctness.rationale: For a continuous parent, the diagonal rank-value covariance is (N-1)G/4 by the identity G=4 Cov(X,F(X)). Exchangeability plus the deterministic rank sum forces every off-diagonal covariance to be -G/4. The resulting matrix acts as NG/4 times the identity on the zero-sum contrast subspace. The usual random-permutation rank covariance matrix and independence of the observations give the two variances, hence the common correlation. Cauchy-Schwarz with F(X) uniform proves the sharp uniform-parent envelope. Exact rational checks independently replay the uniform and beta-family special cases.

value.rationale: The theorem converts a coordinatewise rank-value relationship into a complete structural statement on the (N-1)-dimensional contrast space. It shows that the choice of contrast direction does not change rank-versus-value correlation under the iid continuous null, and yields the practically interpretable consequence that Mann-Whitney and the raw two-sample mean difference have an exact correlation depending only on total sample size and the parent Gini-to-standard-deviation ratio, not on group allocation. The sharp uniform-parent envelope gives a natural extremal interpretation rather than a routine moment calculation.
